title: AsterBank - launch readiness (air-gapped) + signed offline bundles final checklist
summary: Launch-readiness review for AsterBank’s air-gapped Redwood Private rollout using signed offline bundles. Confirmed the documentation set AsterBank needs for internal change control (install/upgrade guide, signature verification steps, key rotation/trust-store updates, break-glass policy). Walked through the final preflight checklist (bundle inspect, signature verify, manifest hash checks, time-skew checks) and clarified support escalation paths and what logs/support bundle data to collect if verification fails (hash mismatch, unknown key after rotation, not-yet-valid due to clock). AsterBank requested a short “offline transport” note (don’t unzip/rezip, verify sha256 before/after transfer) and confirmed they will stage the Redwood public key trust store update in their golden image prior to go-live.
topics: Go-live checklist for signed offline bundles (air-gapped)
Installer version requirements + preflight verification behavior (fail closed)
Trust store / signing key rotation update plan
Break-glass override policy + required audit markers
Support escalation paths + what artifacts to collect
questions: Can we pin to a specific signing key fingerprint for change control, and what’s the process when Redwood rotates keys?
What happens if the cluster clock is off and the signature is ‘not yet valid’?
If verification fails, what exact files do we send Redwood without leaking sensitive config?
Do we need outbound access at any point during install/upgrade (answer: no, installer must not fetch in offline mode)?
action_items: Redwood (Colin): Send AsterBank the final command sequence for offline verification (bundle inspect + preflight) including expected success output and log locations by EOD 2026-01-22.
Redwood (Dev): Share Support escalation matrix for air-gapped installs (severity levels, response targets, and after-hours contact path) by 2026-01-22.
Redwood (Fatima): Provide the doc set list with links/titles for AsterBank change ticket (install guide, FAQ/common errors, key rotation/trust store updates, break-glass policy) by 2026-01-22.
AsterBank (Elena): Validate sha256 of the bundle tarball before and after removable-media transfer in their staging run; report any tooling that modifies files (zip/unzip) by 2026-01-24.
AsterBank (Jonah): Confirm the trust store update procedure is approved and can be applied to the installer host images ahead of go-live by 2026-01-27.
Redwood (Vivek): Confirm required minimum installer version for the GA signed-bundle release and communicate it for AsterBank’s CAB ticket by 2026-01-22.
next_steps: AsterBank to run the “dress rehearsal” upgrade in staging using the signed bundle + verification preflight, then schedule a 30-min follow-up if any verification warnings/errors appear.
Redwood to send consolidated “Launch Readiness Pack” email (commands, docs, escalation, key fingerprint) for CAB submission.
Provisional go-live window remains week of 2026-02-03 pending staging sign-off.
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-01-21
Start time: 4:00 PM ET
Duration: 46 min
Title: AsterBank - launch readiness (air-gapped) + signed offline bundles final checklist

Attendees
Redwood Inference: Markus Klein, Fatima Noor, Colin O'Donnell, Dev Patel, Vivek Kulkarni
AsterBank: Priya Desai, Jonah Miles, Elena Petrova, Samir Khan, Kurt Wallace

Auto Summary (Fireflies)
- Goal: Confirm go-live readiness and last-mile checklist for Redwood Private in AsterBank’s air-gapped environment using signed offline bundles.
- Outcome: Checklist aligned, escalation path confirmed, open items captured (trust store update approval + transport checksum validation).

Transcript

[00:00] Markus Klein: Alright, I think we’re recording. Thanks everyone. This is the last launch readiness call before you submit the CAB ticket, right?

[00:08] Priya Desai: Yep, exactly. We’re basically at “no surprises” mode. We want to confirm the checklist and like, what happens when something fails. And, uh, confirm we have the right doc set.

[00:19] Markus Klein: Makes sense. Today we can do: quick status, then walk the offline bundle verification flow end-to-end, then escalation and what to collect.

[00:28] Fatima Noor: And we’ll explicitly call out the break-glass path. Not recommending it, but we want you to know what it is and what gets logged.

[00:35] Jonah Miles: Great, because our security review asked for that specifically.

[00:39] Vivek Kulkarni: And I can confirm the product side on GA constraints, like minimum installer version and what we’re promising at launch.

[00:47] Elena Petrova: Perfect.

[00:49] Markus Klein: Quick roll call — Priya, Jonah, Elena, Samir, Kurt. Anything else? Cool. Let’s start with where you are. Priya?

[01:01] Priya Desai: We have staging Kubernetes ready, we’ve tested the unsigned bundle process historically. Now we need to validate the signed bundles workflow is stable in air-gapped. Our go-live target is first week Feb. We have an internal freeze around the 31st.

[01:17] Markus Klein: Got it.

[01:18] Kurt Wallace: And network wise, we’re fully disconnected. There is no DNS out, no NTP out. We have an internal time source but it’s… finicky.

[01:28] Colin O'Donnell: That’s important for the signature validity window piece. We’ll cover.

[01:33] Samir Khan: Also for documentation, we need a list of artifacts: what is signed, what is verified, what logs are produced. And a linkable statement of the key rotation process.

[01:45] Fatima Noor: Yep. We’ve got the docs and I’ll package the “names” of them for your change record.

[01:51] Markus Klein: Okay. Let’s jump to the checklist. Colin, can you walk the expected command flow?

[01:57] Colin O'Donnell: Sure. In air-gapped, the flow we recommend is:
1) Validate the bundle file checksum at the transport boundary.
2) Run “bundle inspect” which reads the manifest, lists contained artifacts, and verifies hashes locally.
3) Run installer preflight in offline mode, which verifies signature and trust root and confirms the cluster prereqs.
4) Only then run install/upgrade.

[02:19] Elena Petrova: When you say “checksum at transport boundary,” you mean like before we put it on USB and after?

[02:26] Colin O'Donnell: Exactly. We’ve seen issues where unzip/rezip or some Windows tooling changes line endings or truncates. So: sha256 of the tarball before it leaves the connected staging, and sha256 after it lands in the air-gapped side.

[02:41] Jonah Miles: We actually had that once with a Helm chart tgz. It was… not fun.

[02:45] Colin O'Donnell: Yeah. Same class of problem.

[02:49] Markus Klein: And just to be explicit: the installer is going to fail closed if verification fails. That’s intended.

[02:57] Priya Desai: That’s what we want.

[03:00] Colin O'Donnell: For commands, the current ones you’ll see in docs are along the lines of:
- redwood-private-installer bundle inspect --bundle /path/to/bundle.tar
- redwood-private-installer preflight --offline --bundle /path/to/bundle.tar
It prints signature status, signing key fingerprint, manifest version, and a summary of artifacts verified.

[03:22] Elena Petrova: Is it always a tar? Or can it be a folder?

[03:25] Colin O'Donnell: Our standard is a tarball that unpacks into a deterministic layout. Some customers keep it as a directory, but the signed payload is the manifest plus referenced files. We can support “directory path” too, but your runbooks should be consistent. We’ll send your exact syntax.

[03:42] Vivek Kulkarni: Product requirement is: signature verification must happen during preflight and block the install. So even if someone skips “inspect,” preflight catches it.

[03:51] Jonah Miles: Good.

[03:52] Colin O'Donnell: The signature is detached. So you’ll see manifest.json and manifest.sig (or similar) in the bundle.

[04:01] Samir Khan: Detached is good for us. Easier to explain.

[04:04] Kurt Wallace: Quick question: where does the public key live? Is it embedded, or we provide a file?

[04:10] Colin O'Donnell: By default, the installer has a trust store that can include multiple Redwood public keys. You can also supply an external trust store file if you want to manage it via your config management. That’s the key rotation story.

[04:25] Jonah Miles: We want external. Embedded makes change control tricky.

[04:30] Markus Klein: That’s consistent with what we’ve heard from other regulated customers.

[04:34] Colin O'Donnell: Cool. So the preflight can be pointed at your trust store path. It’ll validate the signing cert / key against that.

[04:45] Priya Desai: Can we pin to a fingerprint in the runbook? Like “if fingerprint != X, stop”?

[04:52] Colin O'Donnell: Yes. It prints the key id / fingerprint. We recommend you record the allowed fingerprints in your CAB documentation.

[05:00] Samir Khan: And what about rotation? That’s the other half. When Redwood rotates, will you break installs?

[05:07] Vivek Kulkarni: If you don’t update trust roots, yes, the verification will fail with “unknown key.” That’s why we do advance notice, overlapping validity, and allow multiple keys in the trust store.

[05:19] Jonah Miles: What’s the notice period?

[05:21] Vivek Kulkarni: Standard is 30 days for planned rotations. Emergency rotations can be shorter, but we document it and provide updated public keys through your support channel.

[05:31] Dev Patel: And from Support side, we’ll also have a runbook entry: “unknown signing key after rotation” with exact remediation.

[05:39] Elena Petrova: Okay. Our internal process can handle planned, but emergency is… harder.

[05:45] Markus Klein: Understood. That’s why the overlapping trust store with multiple keys matters.

[05:51] Colin O'Donnell: Also the manifest includes a build id and release version. The verification output includes those. It makes it easier to correlate.

[06:00] Priya Desai: Great.

[06:02] Markus Klein: Next big one: time. Kurt said no NTP out. Jonah, you had a question around “not yet valid,” right?

[06:10] Jonah Miles: Yep. If the cluster clock is behind, do we just get stuck?

[06:15] Colin O'Donnell: If the signing scheme uses a cert validity window or timestamp checks, a skewed clock can cause “not yet valid” or “expired.” We have two mitigations:
(1) Clear guidance: ensure installer host has a correct time source.
(2) Diagnostic override, not for production, that lets you pass an override time just to confirm it’s a clock issue.

[06:39] Kurt Wallace: Override time sounds dangerous.

[06:42] Fatima Noor: It’s guarded and logged. It’s meant for troubleshooting with Support on the line.

[06:48] Dev Patel: And if you do it, it emits a big warning and a distinct audit marker. We’ll cover what to send us.

[06:56] Samir Khan: For GRC, we’ll need that spelled out. Like “break-glass/time override” is recorded.

[07:03] Markus Klein: Yep.

[07:05] Priya Desai: We actually can sync time internally, but there are windows where it drifts. So we’ll plan to validate time before doing the install.

[07:15] Colin O'Donnell: Perfect. The preflight prints system time as seen by the installer, too.

[07:21] Elena Petrova: Okay.

[07:22] Markus Klein: Next: downgrade/replay. Are you worried about someone rolling back to an old bundle?

[07:29] Jonah Miles: Yes. That’s one of our audit items. We don’t want an operator to “accidentally” install an older one.

[07:36] Colin O'Donnell: The manifest includes a version and we store local install state. Preflight checks if the bundle version is lower than what’s installed and blocks unless you explicitly acknowledge with an override. That override is… again… logged.

[07:52] Samir Khan: That’s good. That’s basically what our control requires.

[07:56] Vivek Kulkarni: Just to confirm, in GA we treat downgrade prevention as on by default.

[08:02] Priya Desai: Great.

[08:04] Markus Klein: Let’s talk about support and escalation. Dev, can you outline severity and what we need when something fails?

[08:11] Dev Patel: Sure. For air-gapped installs, the common failure modes are:
- Signature invalid (manifest.sig mismatch)
- Hash mismatch for an artifact listed in manifest
- Unknown signing key (trust store not updated)
- Not-yet-valid / expired due to time skew
- Bundle incomplete / truncated

[08:31] Dev Patel: For any of those, we’ll ask for:
1) The preflight output (copy/paste)
2) The bundle inspect output
3) Installer logs (path is in output; typically /var/log/redwood/installer/*.log)
4) A “support bundle” archive generated by the installer, which includes metadata and redacted config.

[08:54] Elena Petrova: Do you need the bundle itself? Because that’s complicated for us to move out.

[08:58] Dev Patel: Not by default. We usually don’t. We can triage from manifest and output. If we need a file, we’ll request only the manifest + signature file first, since those are non-sensitive.

[09:10] Jonah Miles: That’s preferred.

[09:12] Markus Klein: Escalation path: during business hours you can go through the standard support portal; for go-live week we’ll set up a named on-call channel. Fatima and Colin will be on the “tiger team.”

[09:25] Fatima Noor: Yeah, we can do a dedicated bridge if needed.

[09:29] Priya Desai: We’ll need the contact matrix in the CAB packet.

[09:33] Dev Patel: I’ll send it. It includes sev1 response targets and who to page.

[09:38] Samir Khan: Response targets, yes.

[09:41] Markus Klein: Now, doc set confirmation. Fatima, can you read out what you’ll send?

[09:46] Fatima Noor: Yep. For your “documentation set” we’ll include:
- Air-gapped installation guide for signed offline bundles (install + upgrade)
- Verification commands reference (inspect/preflight) and expected outputs
- FAQ / common errors (hash mismatch, unknown key, time skew)
- Key rotation + trust store updates guide (planned rotation, emergency rotation)
- Break-glass policy summary (when allowed, approvals, logging)
- Audit events schema reference for verification success/failure (local logs + optional SIEM export)

[10:18] Samir Khan: Great. Add a one-pager “what’s signed” please.

[10:22] Fatima Noor: Yep, we’ll include that.

[10:24] Jonah Miles: And for audit events, what’s in them? We don’t want tokens or prompts.

[10:30] Colin O'Donnell: These are installer verification events, not model inference events. So it’s like: bundle build id, manifest version, result success/fail, error code, signing key id, timestamp, host id (if you allow), and file paths maybe. No prompts.

[10:49] Jonah Miles: Good.

[10:51] Priya Desai: And those logs stay local in air-gapped.

[10:54] Colin O'Donnell: Correct. Export to SIEM is optional if you have your own collector.

[10:59] Kurt Wallace: We do, but it’s internal only.

[11:02] Dev Patel: That’s fine.

[11:04] Markus Klein: Let’s do a quick “tabletop” of the two most likely issues: hash mismatch and unknown key after rotation.

[11:11] Elena Petrova: Hash mismatch is my nightmare.

[11:14] Markus Klein: Colin, what’s your standard triage?

[11:18] Colin O'Donnell: If you see hash mismatch:
- First confirm you’re checking the tarball checksum before/after transfer.
- Confirm you did not extract and repackage.
- Confirm the extraction tool is standard (tar on Linux). Some GUI tools do weird stuff.
- Then run bundle inspect; it will point at the exact file that mismatched.

[11:40] Elena Petrova: We usually unpack on a Windows jump host then move the directory.

[11:44] Colin O'Donnell: That’s the thing we recommend against. Better to transfer as a single tarball and unpack using tar in the air-gapped Linux host.

[11:54] Priya Desai: Elena, we can change that. It’s annoying but doable.

[11:58] Elena Petrova: Yeah, okay.

[12:00] Jonah Miles: Our policy can support that if we scan the tarball.

[12:04] Samir Khan: Yeah, scanning the tarball is easier anyway.

[12:08] Markus Klein: Great. Unknown key after rotation scenario:

[12:12] Dev Patel: If you see “unknown signing key,” it’s almost always trust store not updated. Remediation is: install the updated public key set into your trust store and rerun preflight. For air-gapped, we’d send you the new public key file out-of-band via your secure channel.

[12:29] Jonah Miles: You’ll sign the key file?

[12:31] Vivek Kulkarni: We provide it via a secure channel and it’s also included in the docs set with fingerprints. But yes, we can provide a signed statement or include it in a signed bundle update.

[12:44] Samir Khan: We need a verifiable fingerprint list. If it’s an email attachment that’s not enough.

[12:50] Markus Klein: Understood. We’ll provide fingerprint(s) through the support portal and in the release advisory. And you can verify against what the preflight prints.

[13:01] Priya Desai: That should pass.

[13:03] Kurt Wallace: What about the installer trying to pull images? We have no outbound.

[13:09] Colin O'Donnell: In offline mode it must not attempt to fetch missing artifacts. It will error if something isn’t present in the bundle. That’s by design.

[13:20] Kurt Wallace: Good.

[13:22] Markus Klein: Any last requirements we didn’t cover? Jonah?

[13:27] Jonah Miles: Break-glass. I want to be super clear: what’s the trigger, who approves, what gets logged. Because I can already see someone asking “can we just bypass verification.”

[13:39] Fatima Noor: The answer is: it’s possible but policy-gated. The flag exists for extreme cases. When used, the installer prints a huge warning and writes an audit event “verification_overridden” with reason text. The process is: you open a Support case, we document risk, you get internal approval, and you keep the artifacts for post-incident review.

[14:01] Samir Khan: That’s what we need. The key is “documented risk acceptance.”

[14:05] Dev Patel: And we’ll ask for a follow-up to restore normal verification as soon as possible.

[14:10] Jonah Miles: Okay.

[14:12] Priya Desai: For go-live, we’re not planning to use it.

[14:15] Markus Klein: Great.

[14:17] Colin O'Donnell: One more small thing: please ensure the installer version you use is the one that supports detached signatures and trust store selection.

[14:26] Vivek Kulkarni: Minimum installer version for the GA signed-bundle release will be in the release notes. I’ll confirm the exact number, but you should plan to upgrade the installer first.

[14:38] Elena Petrova: Do we have to upgrade the installer in air-gapped too? Like… that’s another artifact.

[14:43] Colin O'Donnell: Yes, but it’s included as part of your offline distribution. We’ll provide the installer binary and its checksum. Some customers bundle it alongside.

[14:53] Priya Desai: Okay.

[14:55] Markus Klein: We’re at minute 15. Let’s do a fast recap of the “final checklist” items you’ll put in the runbook.

[15:02] Markus Klein: Item 1: verify sha256 before and after transport. Item 2: do not repackage. Item 3: run bundle inspect. Item 4: run preflight offline which verifies signature and trust. Item 5: confirm system time. Item 6: install/upgrade. Item 7: archive outputs and logs for the change record.

[15:25] Priya Desai: Add “confirm trust store fingerprints are current.”

[15:28] Markus Klein: Yes, item 4b.

[15:31] Samir Khan: And “record bundle build id.”

[15:34] Colin O'Donnell: Yep. It prints “bundle build id” and “manifest version.”

[15:40] Kurt Wallace: And ensure no outbound dependencies.

[15:43] Colin O'Donnell: Correct.

[15:46] Markus Klein: Cool.

[15:47] (crosstalk)

[15:48] Elena Petrova: One question: where do the container images come from? Are they in the bundle?

[15:54] Colin O'Donnell: The bundle includes image references plus the offline mechanism you’re using (registry mirror or image tar import) depends on your architecture. For AsterBank, you’re importing into your internal registry, right?

[16:07] Elena Petrova: Yes.

[16:09] Colin O'Donnell: So the bundle includes the list and digests, and your import process must preserve the digests. The manifest verifies those references match what we shipped.

[16:22] Jonah Miles: So if someone swaps an image tag, it fails?

[16:25] Colin O'Donnell: Yes, it should. Tag drift is exactly the supply chain issue we’re preventing.

[16:32] Samir Khan: Great.

[16:34] Markus Klein: Alright, let’s shift to go-live logistics. Priya, what’s your desired support coverage?

[16:41] Priya Desai: For the first install, we want Redwood on standby. Not necessarily on the call, but reachable. And we’d like a 2-hour window where you can respond quickly.

[16:52] Dev Patel: We can do that. We’ll coordinate a time window and put it in the support case.

[16:57] Fatima Noor: Also, for the first upgrade after go-live, same thing.

[17:01] Priya Desai: Yep.

[17:03] Markus Klein: Any procurement/legal or contract items blocking?

[17:07] Samir Khan: Not at this stage. Our only remaining gating item is “artifact signing policy evidence,” which is basically: describe key custody, rotation, and verification in an auditable way.

[17:19] Vivek Kulkarni: We can provide a standard statement for that.

[17:22] Markus Klein: Great.

[17:24] Jonah Miles: One more thing. If we discover a vulnerability and need a hotfix, what’s the story for unsigned bundles? Like does that exist?

[17:34] Markus Klein: There is an exception process, but it’s rare and requires explicit approvals and a risk acceptance. Generally we’ll ship signed hotfixes; unsigned is break-glass at Redwood too.

[17:48] Samir Khan: Okay, as long as it’s formal.

[17:51] Dev Patel: And we’ll document the customer communication path if that ever happens.

[17:56] Priya Desai: Good.

[17:58] Markus Klein: We’re in good shape. I’ll pause for any last questions.

[18:03] (silence)

[18:05] Elena Petrova: Just to confirm: we can run the verify step without touching the cluster? Like on the installer host.

[18:12] Colin O'Donnell: Bundle inspect is purely local. Preflight checks both local and cluster prerequisites. But signature verification is local; it’s done before any cluster changes.

[18:24] Elena Petrova: Great.

[18:26] Priya Desai: Then our next step is a staging dress rehearsal this weekend.

[18:31] Markus Klein: Perfect.

[18:33] Dev Patel: When you do it, please capture the outputs even if it succeeds. It helps for baseline.

[18:39] Jonah Miles: Makes sense.

[18:41] Markus Klein: Alright, we’ll send: (1) command sequence and expected output, (2) escalation matrix, (3) doc set list, (4) minimum installer version confirmation.

[18:55] Priya Desai: Thank you.

[18:56] Fatima Noor: Thanks all.

[18:58] Markus Klein: Stopping recording now.

(Recording ended)

Notes
- Call ended early at ~19 minutes per transcript; remainder of scheduled time was unused.
